title: Worker payment distribution can be visible without restored worker power
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Amazon Flex tip-refund program and eligible delivery drivers; named enforcement and refund-administration records, not a representative worker sample
geography: United States federal consumer-protection enforcement and eligible Amazon Flex drivers

observations.period: 2016 through August 2019 practice; payment administration checked September 17, 2026

current_reissue_route.value: Zelle payments to eligible drivers who did not cash their checks

continued_work_switching_household_recov.value: not observed in public refund record

observations.method: FTC official consent-order, payment-distribution announcement, and current refund-administration page; reported program terms and distribution stages are retained without treating them as a worker-level estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The current page does not publish the complete eligible-driver denominator, current-round success rate, individual amounts, failed delivery, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household recovery, or bargaining outcome. The formal amount and distribution total are not interchangeable.
observations.subgroup: Amazon Flex drivers eligible under the FTC refund program; earlier paid, uncashed, reissued, ineligible, and unknown-status drivers are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Payment receipt may resolve a financial loss for some drivers without changing continued platform use or exit; failure to cash an earlier check may reflect address or payment-channel friction rather than refusal of the remedy.

observations.period: 2024 FTC annual refund report; payment status as of 2024-12-31

denominator.unit: Amazon Flex refund program; administrator-reported eligible-driver population

successful_zelle_payments.unit: drivers; successful Zelle payments after uncashed-check reissue

drivers_full_compensation.unit: drivers reported to have received full compensation

observations.method: Official FTC annual refund report; administrator-reported successful Zelle payments and aggregate payment reach are kept separate from customer-level linkage and downstream work or household outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The report gives aggregate reach and recipient counts as of December 31, 2024 but does not link payment to a named driver's loss, timing, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household recovery, or bargaining outcome.
observations.subgroup: Amazon Flex drivers eligible under the 2021 settlement, including earlier recipients and drivers reached through the Zelle reissue route; no representative worker denominator is inferred.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher aggregate participation after Zelle shows improved payment reach for the program, not that every driver recovered the same loss or changed platform behavior.

related_sources.claim: FTC consent-order amount and future pay/tip disclosure and consent requirements.
FTC reported initial check and PayPal distribution counts and amounts.
FTC annual report records successful Zelle payments, aggregate participation increase, and drivers reported to have received full compensation as of December 31, 2024.

boundary: This record establishes administrator-reported aggregate worker payment reach, including successful Zelle reissue payments and a reported full-compensation count. It does not provide driver-level linkage, average recovery, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household security, bargaining power, trust, collective action, or exit. It is not a representative worker trend or a causal estimate.
